rules.name: is_style_colocated
rules.instructions: Does this stylesheet style COMPONENT behavior via global selectors? Component behavior (hover/active/disabled/selected states; presentation of buttons, rows, triggers) must be styled at the component (Tailwind classes on the element). Global element or attribute selectors - button:not(:disabled), [data-slot=...], .component-class rules that set behavior states - are a second style authority and a violation. NOT violations: @theme token definitions (palette, spacing), base document styles (body, html), non-behavioral resets, and theme assignments to vendor token classes (.hljs-comment etc.).

criteria.true: The file contains at least one global element/attribute selector that styles component behavior (e.g. button:not(:disabled), [data-slot="button"], a .component class setting hover/selected/active states).
criteria.false: No such selector: only @theme tokens, base document styles, non-behavioral resets, and vendor-class theme assignments.

rules.name: is_literal_shared
rules.instructions: The same literal value (string, number, regex) carrying the same meaning at two or more separate places in this TypeScript file should be written once as a named constant in this file and referenced at each place: the identical raw literal at distinct sites is drift waiting to happen. Judge what is observable: identical raw literals at distinct sites where one constant could carry that value to all of them. Brevity of a literal alone is not a defect; imports and identifiers are not literals; recurring words from a shared vocabulary - a styling class string, a prop or option value, an event, sort-key, or mode name, a typeof guard comparison string, an error-code name - are per-site uses of a convention, not one value flowing between sites.

criteria.true: At least one literal value appears as the same raw literal in two or more distinct places where the sites share that value, and no single named constant in this file carries it to all of them.
criteria.false: Every literal that appears in more than one place flows through one named constant defined in this file, or no literal repeats.

rules.name: is_value_tokenized
rules.instructions: In this stylesheet, a value (color, size, spacing, radius, duration, font stack) used at two or more places should be written once as a custom property or an @theme token in this file and referenced at each use. Judge what is observable: the identical raw value at distinct declarations. A repetition across DIFFERENT roles wants one constant per role: coincidental value equality is not sharing - do not merge roles into one token to satisfy this rule. Vendor-class theme assignments and single-use values are not defects. @font-face descriptors are exempt: CSS forbids var() inside them, so their values cannot be tokenized.

criteria.true: At least one value appears as the same raw literal in two or more declarations, and no custom property or @theme token in this file carries it to all of them.
criteria.false: Every value used more than once is defined once in this file as a custom property or @theme token and referenced at its uses, or no value repeats.

rules.name: is_token_role_separated
rules.instructions: In a stylesheet, a custom property names a semantic role - gutter, cell padding, caption line-height, page background - not a value. Two roles whose values coincide today must still own separate custom properties: aliasing one to another by coincidental value couples them, so changing one role silently moves the other. Equal values are not equal semantics. Judge the FILE: does any custom property alias a different role's token, or does one token serve clearly different roles at its use sites? Same-role aliases are by design, not defects: theme variants (.dark re-declaring the same token) and fallback chains var(--a, --b) re-using the same role.

criteria.true: At least one token couples distinct semantic roles: a custom property defined as a reference to another token whose name denotes a different role, or one token consumed by use sites of clearly different roles.
criteria.false: Every custom property names exactly one role: aliases exist only between same-role names (theme-variant re-declarations), and value equality between different roles stays as separate literal definitions.

rules.name: is_palette_tiered
rules.instructions: A tidy stylesheet is organized by responsibility: the custom properties of each declaration block are sorted so that every palette constant (a raw literal - a color, size, or font stack) comes first, then every derived token (a var() reference to another token), in two contiguous runs. Interleaved tokens are the defect: a var()-reference token sitting between constants, or a constant appearing after the derived tokens have begun, means the reader meets a reference before the inputs are done - the palette reads like an unsorted drawer. Organization is declaration ORDER; comments are not structure - a labeled comment neither organizes nor separates, and blank lines are not required. Not part of the ordering: non-custom-property declarations (color-scheme, @font-face font-family), theme-variant re-declarations (.dark overriding derived tokens), and calc() over literals (references no token).

criteria.true: Tokens are interleaved: at least one var()-reference custom property is declared between raw-literal custom properties, or at least one raw-literal custom property is declared after var()-reference tokens have begun.
criteria.false: Tokens are organized by responsibility: all raw-literal constants in one contiguous run first, all var() references in one contiguous run after them - or the block declares only one tier.

rules.name: is_comment_token_note
rules.instructions: In a stylesheet, a comment's only job is to clarify token meaning: what a custom property is for, or why a value is measured rather than scale-named. Judge the FILE: does any comment do more than that?

criteria.true: At least one comment is not a token note: it narrates history, rationale, or process; restates what declaration order already shows; or annotates values with derived numbers (contrast ratios, shade arithmetic) instead of one clause of meaning.
criteria.false: Every comment is one clause of token meaning, or there are no comments.
